thread:
Avi (Support): FYI getting an escalation from a customer (ACME) — after yesterday's req-mapper/v3 rollout they see tool calls either not firing or arriving with empty/missing nested fields. Customer pasted a failing request id: req_0a9f. They say the model output included a function call but our proxy shows an empty args object.
Riley (Oncall): Can you paste the raw model output they sent (or the request payload)? need to know if the function call made it through the runtime.
Avi (Support): Pasting sanitized customer payload below (they redacted PII):
```
{"id":"req_0a9f","model":"redwood-chat-emb-v1","response":{
  "type":"tool_call",
  "tool":"payment_processor",
  "args":{
    "payment":{
      "amount_cents":1000,
      "currency":"USD",
      "method":"card",
      "card":{"last4":"4242"}
    }
  }
}}
```
Avi (Support): But our proxy logged: `tool_invocation_suppressed: normalized_args="{}" path=payment.details`
Riley (Oncall): OK that's consistent with mapper stripping nested objects when a certain flatten rule hits. I just pulled the req-mapper/v3 release notes — we added an aggressive "flatten-nested" optimization to canonicalize arg keys for routing. If a path contains `.` it attempts to map using the new path extractor and can drop the original nested object when it can't find the expected mapping.
Sana (Product): Was that change gated? We thought it was behind a feature flag for a small percent.
Riley (Oncall): It was targeted but the rollout inadvertently included a global default policy for all customer routes due to a config syntax bug in the rollout manifest. So v3 started handling 100% of routes when we flipped the flag.
Avi (Support): Customer reproducer (curl) they ran against our hosted API: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"charge customer"}],"model":"redwood-chat-emb-v1","metadata":{"request_id":"req_0a9f"}}'
```
Riley (Oncall): Quick check I ran on the internal proxy logs for req_0a9f: `proxy: received model tool_call payment_processor args_raw='{"payment":{"amount_cents":1000}}' -> req-mapper: normalized_args='{}' -> tool-proxy: dropping invocation (no args match signature)`
Sana (Product): Impact? How many customers affected?
Riley (Oncall): So far only two reports — ACME (high priority) and one other. But the mapper logs show ~120 invocations/day where normalized_args became empty after v3 rollout. Most are no-ops, but any nested-arg tool is at risk.
Avi (Support): Customer is blocked — their payments integration retries are failing. They asked for immediate mitigation (rollback or bypass).
Riley (Oncall): Suggested immediate mitigations: 1) rollback req-mapper to v2 for all routes (fastest) 2) patch config to bypass req-mapper for toolcall routes only 3) hotfix to stop flattening if nested objects present. I can trigger rollback now if infra approves.
Sana (Product): Let's avoid global rollback if possible. Apply a temporary bypass rule for toolcall routes (match: response.type=="tool_call") and route those around req-mapper. Do that as a stopgap and then roll forward the mapper fix.
Riley (Oncall): Working on bypass rule now. Command I'm running: `kubectl patch cm req-mapper-config --type=json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/bypassRules/0","value":{"match":"response.type==\\\"tool_call\\\"","reason":"restore toolcall args"}}]' -n infra`
infra-bot: deploy started for config patch req-mapper-bypass-2026-03-16T18:22Z by Riley. Status: rolling update to 3/3 pods.
Riley (Oncall): Patch applied and rollout completed. I reprocessed a sample request through the proxy and now normalized_args contains the nested object again. Example log: `proxy: received model tool_call payment_processor args_raw='{"payment":{...}}' -> req-mapper: bypassed -> tool-proxy: invoked payment_processor args present`
Avi (Support): I notified ACME and asked them to retry. They confirmed their webhook retried and the payment hit their backend successfully.
Sana (Product): Good. Next steps: 1) revert the accidental global policy in the rollout manifest 2) add unit tests for nested arg preservation 3) ship mapper v3 patch that disables flattening unless explicitly enabled per-route 4) postmortem and customer communication.
Riley (Oncall): I'll open the incident and attach logs + repro steps. Assigning to eng-runtime and eng-platform to fix the mapper behavior and rollout manifest.
Avi (Support): Adding ACME's contact to the incident notes and preparing an apology + incident summary to send once we have root cause and fix ETA.
Sana (Product): ETA for patch?
Riley (Oncall): I'll aim for a low-risk patch for v3 by EOD PST, otherwise we keep bypass until patch is validated.
Avi (Support): Thanks — keeping thread updated with any customer replies. :thumbsup:
